paragraphs.text: I must needs glory, though it is not expedient; but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ· οὐ συμφέρον μέν, ἐλεύσομαι δὲ εἰς ὀπτασίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεις κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: Kauchasthai dei· ou sympheron men, eleusomai de eis optasias kai apokalypseis kyriou.

paragraphs.text: I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not; or whether out of the body, I know not; God knoweth), such a one caught up even to the third heaven.
paragraphs.original: οἶδα ἄνθρωπον ἐν Χριστῷ πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων— εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα, εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν— ἁρπαγέντα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: oida anthrōpon en Christō pro etōn dekatessarōn— eite en sōmati ouk oida, eite ektos tou sōmatos ouk oida, ho theos oiden— harpagenta ton toiouton heōs tritou ouranou.

paragraphs.text: And I know such a man (whether in the body, or apart from the body, I know not; God knoweth),
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἶδα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἄνθρωπον— εἴτε ἐν σώματι εἴτε χωρὶς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν—
paragraphs.translit: kai oida ton toiouton anthrōpon— eite en sōmati eite chōris tou sōmatos ouk oida, ho theos oiden—

paragraphs.text: how that he was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἡρπάγη εἰς τὸν παράδεισον καὶ ἤκουσεν ἄρρητα ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀνθρώπῳ λαλῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: hoti hērpagē eis ton paradeison kai ēkousen arrēta rhēmata ha ouk exon anthrōpō lalēsai.

paragraphs.text: On behalf of such a one will I glory: but on mine own behalf I will not glory, save in [my] weaknesses.
paragraphs.original: ὑπὲρ τοῦ τοιούτου καυχήσομαι, ὑπὲρ δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ καυχήσομαι εἰ μὴ ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις.
paragraphs.translit: hyper tou toioutou kauchēsomai, hyper de emautou ou kauchēsomai ei mē en tais astheneiais.

paragraphs.text: For if I should desire to glory, I shall not be foolish; for I shall speak the truth: but I forbear, lest any man should account of me above that which he seeth me [to be], or heareth from me.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γὰρ θελήσω καυχήσασθαι, οὐκ ἔσομαι ἄφρων, ἀλήθειαν γὰρ ἐρῶ· φείδομαι δέ, μή τις εἰς ἐμὲ λογίσηται ὑπὲρ ὃ βλέπει με ἢ ἀκούει τι ἐξ ἐμοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ean gar thelēsō kauchēsasthai, ouk esomai aphrōn, alētheian gar erō· pheidomai de, mē tis eis eme logisētai hyper ho blepei me ē akouei ti ex emou,

paragraphs.text: And by reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted overmuch, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, that I should not be exalted overmuch.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῶν ἀποκαλύψεων. διὸ ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι, ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί, ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, ἵνα με κολαφίζῃ, ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai tē hyperbolē tōn apokalypseōn. dio hina mē hyperairōmai, edothē moi skolops tē sarki, angelos Satana, hina me kolaphizē, hina mē hyperairōmai.

paragraphs.text: Concerning this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.
paragraphs.original: ὑπὲρ τούτου τρὶς τὸν κύριον παρεκάλεσα ἵνα ἀποστῇ ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hyper toutou tris ton kyrion parekalesa hina apostē apʼ emou·

paragraphs.text: And he hath said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for [my] power is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι· Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου· ἡ γὰρ δύναμις ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελεῖται. ἥδιστα οὖν μᾶλλον καυχήσομαι ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις μου, ἵνα ἐπισκηνώσῃ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eirēken moi· Arkei soi hē charis mou· hē gar dynamis en astheneia teleitai. hēdista oun mallon kauchēsomai en tais astheneiais mou, hina episkēnōsē epʼ eme hē dynamis tou Christou.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ`s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
paragraphs.original: διὸ εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις, ἐν ὕβρεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν διωγμοῖς καὶ στενοχωρίαις, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ, τότε δυνατός εἰμι.
paragraphs.translit: dio eudokō en astheneiais, en hybresin, en anankais, en diōgmois kai stenochōriais, hyper Christou· hotan gar asthenō, tote dynatos eimi.

paragraphs.text: I am become foolish: ye compelled me; for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing was I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I am nothing.
paragraphs.original: Γέγονα ἄφρων· ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε· ἐγὼ γὰρ ὤφειλον ὑφʼ ὑμῶν συνίστασθαι. οὐδὲν γὰρ ὑστέρησα τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων, εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι·
paragraphs.translit: Gegona aphrōn· hymeis me ēnankasate· egō gar ōpheilon hyphʼ hymōn synistasthai. ouden gar hysterēsa tōn hyperlian apostolōn, ei kai ouden eimi·

paragraphs.text: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, by signs and wonders and mighty works.
paragraphs.original: τὰ μὲν σημεῖα τοῦ ἀποστόλου κατειργάσθη ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν πάσῃ ὑπομονῇ, σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ δυνάμεσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ta men sēmeia tou apostolou kateirgasthē en hymin en pasē hypomonē, sēmeiois te kai terasin kai dynamesin.

paragraphs.text: For what is there wherein ye were made inferior to the rest of the churches, except [it be] that I myself was not a burden to you? forgive me this wrong.
paragraphs.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν ὃ ἡσσώθητε ὑπὲρ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐκκλησίας, εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ οὐ κατενάρκησα ὑμῶν; χαρίσασθέ μοι τὴν ἀδικίαν ταύτην.
paragraphs.translit: ti gar estin ho hēssōthēte hyper tas loipas ekklēsias, ei mē hoti autos egō ou katenarkēsa hymōn; charisasthe moi tēn adikian tautēn.

paragraphs.text: Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be a burden to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
paragraphs.original: Ἰδοὺ τρίτον τοῦτο ἑτοίμως ἔχω ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐ καταναρκήσω· οὐ γὰρ ζητῶ τὰ ὑμῶν ἀλλὰ ὑμᾶς, οὐ γὰρ ὀφείλει τὰ τέκνα τοῖς γονεῦσιν θησαυρίζειν, ἀλλὰ οἱ γονεῖς τοῖς τέκνοις.
paragraphs.translit: Idou triton touto hetoimōs echō elthein pros hymas, kai ou katanarkēsō· ou gar zētō ta hymōn alla hymas, ou gar opheilei ta tekna tois goneusin thēsaurizein, alla hoi goneis tois teknois.

paragraphs.text: And I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἥδιστα δαπανήσω καὶ ἐκδαπανηθήσομαι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν. εἰ περισσοτέρως ὑμᾶς ἀγαπῶν, ἧσσον ἀγαπῶμαι;
paragraphs.translit: egō de hēdista dapanēsō kai ekdapanēthēsomai hyper tōn psychōn hymōn. ei perissoterōs hymas agapōn, hēsson agapōmai;

paragraphs.text: But be it so, I did not myself burden you; but, being crafty, I caught you with guile.
paragraphs.original: ἔστω δέ, ἐγὼ οὐ κατεβάρησα ὑμᾶς· ἀλλὰ ὑπάρχων πανοῦργος δόλῳ ὑμᾶς ἔλαβον.
paragraphs.translit: estō de, egō ou katebarēsa hymas· alla hyparchōn panourgos dolō hymas elabon.

paragraphs.text: Did I take advantage of you by any one of them whom I have sent unto you?
paragraphs.original: μή τινα ὧν ἀπέσταλκα πρὸς ὑμᾶς, διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπλεονέκτησα ὑμᾶς;
paragraphs.translit: mē tina hōn apestalka pros hymas, diʼ autou epleonektēsa hymas;

paragraphs.text: I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? walked we not in the same spirit? [walked we] not in the same steps?
paragraphs.original: παρεκάλεσα Τίτον καὶ συναπέστειλα τὸν ἀδελφόν· μήτι ἐπλεονέκτησεν ὑμᾶς Τίτος; οὐ τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι περιεπατήσαμεν; οὐ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἴχνεσιν;
paragraphs.translit: parekalesa Titon kai synapesteila ton adelphon· mēti epleonektēsen hymas Titos; ou tō autō pneumati periepatēsamen; ou tois autois ichnesin;

paragraphs.text: Ye think all this time that we are excusing ourselves unto you. In the sight of God speak we in Christ. But all things, beloved, [are] for your edifying.
paragraphs.original: Πάλαι δοκεῖτε ὅτι ὑμῖν ἀπολογούμεθα; κατέναντι θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν. τὰ δὲ πάντα, ἀγαπητοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν οἰκοδομῆς,
paragraphs.translit: Palai dokeite hoti hymin apologoumetha; katenanti theou en Christō laloumen. ta de panta, agapētoi, hyper tēs hymōn oikodomēs,

paragraphs.text: For I fear, lest by any means, when I come, I should find you not such as I would, and should myself be found of you such as ye would not; lest by any means [there should be] strife, jealousy, wraths, factions, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults;
paragraphs.original: φοβοῦμαι γὰρ μή πως ἐλθὼν οὐχ οἵους θέλω εὕρω ὑμᾶς, κἀγὼ εὑρεθῶ ὑμῖν οἷον οὐ θέλετε, μή πως ἔρις, ζῆλος, θυμοί, ἐριθεῖαι, καταλαλιαί, ψιθυρισμοί, φυσιώσεις, ἀκαταστασίαι·
paragraphs.translit: phoboumai gar mē pōs elthōn ouch hoious thelō heurō hymas, kagō heurethō hymin hoion ou thelete, mē pōs eris, zēlos, thymoi, eritheiai, katalaliai, psithyrismoi, physiōseis, akatastasiai·

paragraphs.text: lest again when I come my God should humble me before you, and I should mourn for many of them that have sinned heretofore, and repented not of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they committed.
paragraphs.original: μὴ πάλιν ἐλθόντος μου ταπεινώσῃ με ὁ θεός μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ πενθήσω πολλοὺς τῶν προημαρτηκότων καὶ μὴ μετανοησάντων ἐπὶ τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ ἀσελγείᾳ ᾗ ἔπραξαν.
paragraphs.translit: mē palin elthontos mou tapeinōsē me ho theos mou pros hymas, kai penthēsō pollous tōn proēmartēkotōn kai mē metanoēsantōn epi tē akatharsia kai porneia kai aselgeia hē epraxan.
